Most people don’t fail PySpark interviews because they don’t know it.
They fail because they blank out on the basics.
In interviews, it’s rarely about writing complex pipelines.
It’s about how quickly you can recall and apply the right function.
And under pressure… even simple things feel hard.
A quick mental checklist that actually helps:
𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮
→ creating / modifying columns
→ filtering rows
→ handling duplicates
𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗯𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘀
→ joins (and when to use which type)
→ union vs unionByName
→ partitioning decisions
𝗔𝗴𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗴𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀
→ group + aggregate patterns
→ list vs set behavior
→ quick profiling of data
𝗛𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹-𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗺𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀
→ null values
→ conditional logic
→ inconsistent data
𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗼𝗻
→ window functions (ranking, ordering)
→ date transformations
→ working with nested / JSON data
Here’s the catch:
Knowing the function ≠ clearing the interview.
What actually stands out is:
• when you use it
• why you use it
• how it impacts performance
That’s the difference between:
“I know PySpark”
vs
“I can solve problems using PySpark”
If you’re preparing right now, don’t just practice syntax.
Practice thinking.
That’s what interviewers are really testing.
